$comment: The lifecycle half of 'may a reader see this article', written once and run
Only the clause both sides actually evaluate is listed here -- status and
publishedAt. The backend additionally decides audience (DepartmentMatcher)
and lets content administrators through; the frontend additionally hides
is_draft rows. Those are not duplicated between the two and so are not
compared here; each is tested on its own side.
publishedAt is relative on purpose. The backend compares against
TbilisiTime.now() (a fixed +04:00 offset) and the browser against the
viewer's local clock, so the two agree for a viewer in Georgia and can
differ by hours for one elsewhere. Every case below is a full day either
side of now, which keeps the fixture about the rule rather than about the
clock. That boundary difference is real and deliberate -- the product is
Georgia-only -- but it is the reason not to add a 'one second ago' case.

cases.name: published, with no date at all
cases.why: published short-circuits before the date is looked at

cases.name: published, with a future date
cases.why: same short-circuit; status wins over a stale future date

cases.name: scheduled, moment has passed
cases.why: nothing flips the status column, so the date is the truth

cases.name: scheduled, with no date
cases.why: a schedule with no moment never arrives

cases.name: an unrecognised status
cases.why: both sides allow-list rather than deny-list, so a new status is invisible until it is handled
